edges.mechanism: Combined theanine+caffeine improves attention switching, vigilance and alertness more than placebo (caffeine dose dominates); theanine blunts caffeine-induced BP rise, jitteriness/anxiety and tachycardia.
edges.evidence: MAs of RCTs (Camfield 2014; Payne 2025) plus crossover RCTs; some trials show no added benefit over either alone; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Both used as sleep aids; possible additive sleep-promoting effect. Head-to-head RCT: melatonin 3 mg superior to theanine 200 mg, both better than placebo. No combination study.
edges.evidence: Single RCT (n=120) head-to-head; combination untested; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Glycine and theanine are both sleep-promoting amino acids; a blend containing both shortened sleep latency and raised sleep efficiency; theanine reported to induce glycine release and to raise a glycine-overlapping serum peak in mice.
edges.evidence: Multi-ingredient crossover RCT (n=16) cannot isolate components; animal data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Green tea extracts contain theanine plus catechins; extract hepatotoxicity is dose-dependent and tied to EGCG/catechin bolus dosing, not to theanine. Stacking adds catechin exposure and duplicates theanine.
edges.evidence: Systematic review of toxicology and 159 human studies (safe EGCG level 338 mg/d as bolus); narrative review flags hepatotoxicity of GTE

edges.mechanism: Commonly co-formulated for sleep. A theanine+GABA+magnesium+SAMe product improved menopausal sleep disturbance, but an evening MgT+theanine+apigenin blend had minimal effects.
edges.evidence: Two multi-ingredient RCTs with conflicting results; components not isolated; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: GABA/theanine mixture synergistically decreased sleep latency and increased sleep duration in rodents; GABA 700 mg + theanine 200 mg improved PSQI in a single-arm human study.
edges.evidence: Animal data plus uncontrolled human study (n=19); very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Piperine-containing formulation increased theanine plasma concentrations in rats by increasing intestinal blood flow.

Theanine lowered the hypnotic ED50 of pentobarbital and enhanced its anticonvulsant action in mice, and acted additively/synergistically with midazolam in rats; in humans 200 mg showed no acute anxiolytic effect comparable to alprazolam.
edges.evidence: Animal studies; one human comparison study; additive sedation not demonstrated in humans

edges.mechanism: Theanine attenuates stress- and caffeine-induced BP rises in humans and lowers BP in hypertensive rats at very high doses; additive BP lowering theoretically possible.
edges.evidence: Small crossover RCTs and rat study; no interaction study; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Adjunctive 250-400 mg/d theanine with antipsychotics (incl. risperidone) reduced positive, negative, activation and anxiety symptoms without increasing side effects or extrapyramidal symptoms.
edges.evidence: 3 small RCTs plus open-label study and SR; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Adjunctive 200 mg/d theanine with sertraline improved HDRS response/remission with comparable side effects; adjunct to stable antidepressants in GAD showed no anxiolytic benefit but no safety signal.
Theanine with caffeine improved attention in ADHD comparably to methylphenidate (compared, not combined); boys on stimulants took 400 mg/d theanine without significant AEs.
edges.evidence: Small RCTs in ADHD; no formal combination study

edges.with: anthracycline and platinum chemotherapy (doxorubicin, idarubicin, cisplatin)
edges.mechanism: In tumor-bearing mice theanine increased tumor doxorubicin/idarubicin concentrations (glutamate-transporter/GS-X pump inhibition) and antitumor effect while reducing myelosuppression; reduced cisplatin nephrotoxicity in mice. Human relevance unknown.
edges.evidence: Animal and in vitro data only; no human data

edges.mechanism: No lactation data; LactMed advises avoiding supplemental theanine when nursing a newborn or preterm infant (half-life ~1 h; tea-level intake likely acceptable).
edges.evidence: Expert database guidance; no human data

edges.mechanism: No human pregnancy safety data; only animal (mouse gestational obesity) and rat toxicology studies.
edges.evidence: Absence of human data; animal studies only

edges.mechanism: In mice theanine produced a peak overlapping glycine in PITC-derivatized amino-acid analysis; theanine is hydrolyzed to glutamate and ethylamine, which rise transiently in plasma.
edges.evidence: Mouse analytical observation and human PK study; clinical relevance unknown
